course_learning_outcomes.text: Relate a deeper understanding of the history of artificial intelligence (AI) and its foundations.
Understand intelligent agents and their operational contexts.
Apply basic principles of AI in solutions that require problem solving, inference, perception, knowledge representation, and learning.

additional_text: TLO1. Distinguish the history of AI and its foundations.
TLO2. Classify the structures of agents and its environments.
TLO3. Differentiate between various types of intelligent agents (e.g., simple reflex agents, model- based agents, goal-based agents, utility-based agents).
TLO4. Describe different types of environments in which intelligent agents operate (e.g., fully observable vs. partially observable, deterministic vs. stochastic, episodic vs. sequential).
TLO5. Explain the architecture of intelligent agents, including the perception, reasoning, and action components.
TLO6. Define problem solving in the context of artificial intelligence.
TLO7. Differentiate between various types of problems (e.g., deterministic vs. stochastic, single- agent vs. multi-agent).
TLO8. Describe different search strategies used in AI, including uninformed (blind) search and informed (heuristic) search.
TLO9. Compare and contrast various search algorithms such as breadth-first search, depth-first search, uniform-cost search, and A* search.

course_learning_outcomes.text: Recognize the concepts of artificial intelligence in different fields.
Discover the importance of technology by creating different applications.
Demonstrate 21st century skills in all learning activities.

additional_text: TLO10. Apply different techniques to create games and applications.
TLO11. Classify learning from examples, knowledge in learning and reinforcement learning.
TLO12. Apply genetic algorithm to solve optimization problems.
TLO14. Apply the different topics you learned in AI to come up with a new innovation.
TLO15. Collaboration, Skilled Communication, Knowledge Construction, Self-Regulation, Real-World ProblemSolving, Use of ICT (not part of topic, but integrated in assessments)
